Function [CC]: FUNCTION: Photoreceptor required for image-forming vision at low light intensity. While most salt water fish species use retinal as chromophore, most freshwater fish use 3-dehydroretinal, or a mixture of retinal and 3-dehydroretinal. Light-induced isomerization of 11-cis to all-trans retinal triggers a conformational change that activates signaling via G proteins. Subsequent receptor phosphorylation mediates displacement of the bound G protein alpha subunit by arrestin and terminates signaling. {ECO:0000256|ARBA:ARBA00095979}.

Function [CC]: FUNCTION: Photoreceptor required for image-forming vision at low light intensity. While most salt water fish species use retinal as chromophore, most freshwater fish use 3-dehydroretinal, or a mixture of retinal and 3-dehydroretinal. Light-induced isomerization of 11-cis to all-trans retinal triggers a conformational change that activates signaling via G proteins. Subsequent receptor phosphorylation mediates displacement of the bound G protein alpha subunit by arrestin and terminates signaling. {ECO:0000256|ARBA:ARBA00095979}.

Function [CC]: FUNCTION: Inhibitory gamma subunit of the cone-specific cGMP phosphodiesterase (PDE6) complex which hydrolyzes 3',5'-cyclic GMP in the phototransduction cascade. The PDE6 holoenzyme consists of two catalytic alpha subunits (PDE6C) and two inhibitory gamma subunits (PDE6H). Light-activated GNAT2 relieves gamma subunit-mediated inhibition, allowing the catalytic subunits to hydrolyze cGMP and mediate visual signal transduction and amplification. The resulting decrease in cytosolic cGMP levels triggers the closure of cGMP-gated cation channels at the plasma membrane, leading to hyperpolarization of cone photoreceptors. Inhibition by the gamma subunit is relatively dynamic and less tightly coupled than in rods, allowing transient access to the catalytic pocket and facilitating the rapid phototransduction kinetics characteristic of cones. {ECO:0000256|ARBA:ARBA00097266}.

Function [CC]: FUNCTION: Inhibitory gamma subunit of the cone-specific cGMP phosphodiesterase (PDE6) complex which hydrolyzes 3',5'-cyclic GMP in the phototransduction cascade. The PDE6 holoenzyme consists of two catalytic alpha subunits (PDE6C) and two inhibitory gamma subunits (PDE6H). Light-activated GNAT2 relieves gamma subunit-mediated inhibition, allowing the catalytic subunits to hydrolyze cGMP and mediate visual signal transduction and amplification. The resulting decrease in cytosolic cGMP levels triggers the closure of cGMP-gated cation channels at the plasma membrane, leading to hyperpolarization of cone photoreceptors. Inhibition by the gamma subunit is relatively dynamic and less tightly coupled than in rods, allowing transient access to the catalytic pocket and facilitating the rapid phototransduction kinetics characteristic of cones. {ECO:0000256|ARBA:ARBA00097266}.

The PDE6 holoenzyme consists of two catalytic alpha subunits (PDE6C) and two inhibitory gamma subunits (PDE6H). Light-activated GNAT2 relieves gamma subunit-mediated inhibition, allowing the catalytic subunits to hydrolyze cGMP and mediate visual signal transduction and amplification. The resulting decrease in cytosolic cGMP levels triggers the closure of cGMP-gated cation channels at the plasma membrane, leading to hyperpolarization of cone photoreceptors. Inhibition by the gamma subunit is relatively dynamic and less tightly coupled than in rods, allowing transient access to the catalytic pocket and facilitating the rapid phototransduction kinetics characteristic of cones. {ECO:0000256|ARBA:ARBA00097266}.
